extracted.intended_audience: tech-industry readers, publishers, and policymakers concerned with platform curation and media bias
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating how Apple News selects, surfaces, and ranks publisher content — including the balance of algorithmic personalization and human editorial decisions — and the transparency, fairness, and regulatory compliance of those practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality of editorial selections
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether editorial selections accurately reflect the full diversity of participating publishers and do not favor certain political viewpoints over others (claims that the platform’s editorial curation may favor certain political viewpoints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns arise because Apple News is a hybrid of algorithmic and human editorial choices; debates focus on whether editorial selections fairly represent participating outlets. Regulators are reviewing neutrality claims but the inquiry described is an internal evaluation request rather than formal enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid curation model: algorithmic personalization vs human editorial selections
rubrics_metrics.description: How the platform combines algorithmic recommendations (personalization based on reading behavior, topic interests, regional relevance) with human-assembled editorial collections, featured stories, and curated topic pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Featured stories and curated collections are often assembled by editorial teams while recommendation systems personalize additional articles. Evaluations should consider roles and boundaries between automated ranking and editorial promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection criteria: journalistic quality, relevance, and reader interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple has historically stated that editorial selections are based on 'journalistic quality, relevance, and reader interest' rather than political alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing specific placements or alleged bias, use these stated criteria as the platform’s purported standards; examine whether selections demonstrably align with or depart from these factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility under publisher/platform guidelines (featured placements, advertising, subscriptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers participating in Apple News agree to platform guidelines that define eligibility for featured placements, advertising participation, and subscription offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether a publisher met stated eligibility conditions before challenging placement decisions. Platform guidelines are a primary source for judging whether a placement was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility determinants: publication frequency, editorial quality metrics, engagement performance, and technical integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Visibility within the app may depend on factors including publication frequency, editorial quality metrics, engagement performance, and technical integration with Apple’s publishing tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operational factors often 'operate behind the scenes'; assessments should account for their potential impact and request documentation when evaluating claims of unfair treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of ranking and editorial processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of transparency available to participating publishers about how featured placements and recommendations are determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency can be improved via published transparency reports, clearer documentation explaining featured-placement determination, and public disclosures of ranking and editorial policies. Lack of clarity is an identified source of publisher concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in application of platform rules across publishers (marketplace fairness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether platform rules and editorial guidelines are applied consistently across different publishers, avoiding arbitrary or discriminatory treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators (e.g., the FTC) are reviewing whether inconsistent application could raise consumer-protection or marketplace fairness issues. Audits and internal reviews should examine cross-publisher consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher recourse: appeals processes and feedback channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and quality of publisher-facing appeals processes, feedback channels, and communications about content-selection decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technology companies have responded to scrutiny by expanding publisher appeals processes and feedback channels; effectiveness of these mechanisms is a criterion for evaluating governance and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal review mechanisms and content-selection audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence and rigor of internal review mechanisms and audits designed to evaluate whether editorial guidelines and platform rules are being applied consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms are increasingly formalizing internal reviews and audits to address concerns; assessments should examine whether audits are regular, independent, and lead to remedial action when inconsistencies are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of editorial placement on publisher readership and operations
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which featured placements and editorial promotion materially affect publisher readership and business outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because featured placements can significantly increase readership, curation policies are an important operational consideration for publishers; this impact is part of why publishers request greater visibility into ranking systems.
